correctness.rationale: The base-\(b\) expansions are exact: \(b(2b-3)=(1,b-3,0)_b\) has digit sum \(b-2\), while \((b-2)(2b-3)=(1,b-7,6)_b\) has digit sum \(b\) for \(b\ge8\). The resulting products are equal. The coprimalities \(\gcd(b,2b-3)=\gcd(b,3)\) and \(\gcd(b-2,2b-3)=1\) prove squarefreeness under the stated hypotheses. For \(b\equiv5\pmod{36}\), the prime squares \(4\) and \(9\) are excluded automatically; for each prime \(p\ge5\), the three bad divisibilities occupy at most three residue classes modulo \(p^2\) inside the progression. The union bound and \(\sum_{p\ge5}p^{-2}<6/25\) give lower density at least \(7/900\). The packaged checker independently replays the digit sums, squarefreeness, and collision over a large finite range.
